summary: _sqlite_udf.py is a clean, minimal set of @proxy wrappers with no DES issues. _sqlite_udf_helpers.py is well-factored but carries notable duplication: the agg==0 and slot[0]==0 init+finalize/value branches in _XFINAL_SRC/_XVALUE_SRC are byte-identical, and the whole codegen scaffolding (digest->anchor->materialize->compile->exec, _stem, _prepare callbacks, orphan-sweep import block) is copy-pasted between this module and the sibling _sqlite_tvf.py. All findings are local, low-risk simplifications; nothing is a correctness defect.

findings.title: Identical init+finalize branches duplicated in _XFINAL_SRC (and _value in _XVALUE_SRC)
findings.claim: In _XFINAL_SRC the agg==0 branch (lines 116-125) and the slot[0]==0 branch (lines 128-137) are byte-for-byte identical: each runs `_state = _init()` guarded by a try/except reporting 'error in user init callback', then `_finalize(_state, ctx)` guarded by a try/except reporting 'error in user finalize callback', then returns. The same duplication appears in _XVALUE_SRC (lines 165-174 vs 177-186) for the _value path. This is a maintenance hazard: a future fix to the no-state finalize/value path must be applied in two places or they silently drift.
findings.evidence: Lines 116-125 and 128-137 read identically except for the preceding `if agg == 0:` vs `if slot[0] == 0:`. Both call `_init()` then `_finalize(_state, ctx)` with the same two error strings and a trailing `return`. The two conditions (agg==0 means SQLite never allocated the slot; slot[0]==0 means it allocated but no step ran) both mean 'empty group', so they intentionally do the same thing -- which is exactly why the body should be shared rather than copied.
findings.recommendation: Collapse the two empty-group branches into one: compute `slot0 = 0 if agg == 0 else carray(...)[0]` (or branch only to obtain slot0) and run a single init+finalize block when `slot0 == 0`. Local, low-risk; the generated semantics are unchanged. Apply the same collapse to _XVALUE_SRC.

findings.title: Codegen scaffolding duplicated between _sqlite_udf_helpers.py and _sqlite_tvf.py
findings.claim: The dynamic-codegen scaffolding is copy-pasted between this module and the sibling _sqlite_tvf.py: (a) the `_ANCHOR_SUBDIR = ...; _orphan_anchor_sweep(_ANCHOR_SUBDIR)` import-time block; (b) `_stem(prefix, name)` which sanitizes a SQL name with `''.join(c if c.isalnum() else '_' for c in name)`; (c) the digest->anchor->materialize->compile->exec sequence in `_compile_callbacks` (lines 221-235) which is structurally identical to `_compile_xfilter` in _sqlite_tvf.py (lines 360-372), down to the `ns = {**globals(), ...}` seeding and the `# nosec B102` exec; (d) the `is_jitted` passthrough / `njit(fn)` wrap in `_prepare_callbacks` vs `_prepare_fn` in _sqlite_tvf.py. Two near-identical copies of JIT-codegen plumbing will drift.
findings.evidence: _sqlite_udf_helpers.py line 249: `return prefix + ''.join(c if c.isalnum() else '_' for c in name)`; _sqlite_tvf.py line 425: `return 'tvf_' + ''.join(c if c.isalnum() else '_' for c in name)` -- same sanitizer. _compile_callbacks (lines 230-234): `ns = {**globals(), '_state_type': state_type, **fns}; anchor = _anchor_path(...); _materialize_anchor(anchor, code_txt); code = compile(code_txt, str(anchor), mode='exec'); exec(code, ns)` matches _compile_xfilter (lines 367-371) line-for-line in shape. Both modules also repeat `_orphan_anchor_sweep(_ANCHOR_SUBDIR)` at import (this module line 85; _sqlite_tvf.py line 78).
findings.recommendation: Hoist a small shared codegen helper into numbox/utils/preprocessing.py (which already owns _anchor_path/_materialize_anchor/_orphan_anchor_sweep): e.g. a `_stem(prefix, name)` sanitizer and a `compile_anchored(subdir, stem, code_txt, ns) -> ns` that does anchor+materialize+compile+exec. Both _sqlite_udf_helpers and _sqlite_tvf then compose it. Low risk; keeps the digest/template generation (which legitimately differs per module) local.

findings.title: Repeated try/except + sqlite3_result_error error-report idiom across templates
findings.claim: The identical 4-line idiom `try: <call> except Exception: sqlite3_result_error(ctx, get_unicode_data_p("error in user <role> callback"), -1); return` is hand-written about ten times across _XSTEP_SRC/_XFINAL_SRC/_XINVERSE_SRC/_XVALUE_SRC, differing only in the callback-name string and whether a trailing `return` follows. Adding context (e.g. switching from -1/SQLITE_TRANSIENT to a structured error code, or appending the numba exception text) means editing every copy. The message strings ('error in user init/step/finalize/inverse/value callback') are also literals scattered through generated source rather than parameterized.
findings.evidence: Compare lines 100-103 (init in xStep), 107-108 (step), 118-120 (init in xFinal), 123-124 (finalize), 130-132 (init dup), 135-136 (finalize dup), 140-141 (finalize live), 154-157 (inverse), 166-168/171-173/178-180/184-185/188-190 (value paths) -- all the same `except Exception: sqlite3_result_error(ctx, get_unicode_data_p("error in user X callback"), -1)` shape with only X varying.
findings.recommendation: Lower priority than DES-sqlite_udf-1/2 and partly mitigated once those collapses land. If pursued, factor the report into a generated `@njit` helper `_report_err(ctx, msg_p)` baked once into the exec namespace, or template the role string -- but only if it does not obscure the inlined codegen. Note risk/benefit: marginal; do not refactor for taste alone.
